name: Save Our Seas Foundation Small Grants
summary: Annual small grants for short start-up projects on sharks, rays, skates, sawfishes and chimaeras, aimed at early-career scientists, emerging conservation practitioners and community-led initiatives in any country.
reporting: Grantees submit a final report on the SOSF template, with a financial summary of how the funds were used, no later than 90 days after the project ends.

eligibility.rule: Early-career (degree within 5 years), an emerging conservation practitioner, or a community-led initiative
Has not already received two SOSF Small Grants
Did not receive a first SOSF Small Grant in the previous year
Budget asks for no salaries, conference attendance or publication costs

documents: Recent CV of the project leader (and co-leader)
Letter of recommendation, from the supervisor if there is one

status.quote: Stage I: is CLOSED and will open again mid-March 2027

administered_by.quote: Save Our Seas Foundation has supported and funded over 300 research, conservation and education Projects worldwide

applicant_types.quote: dedicated to early-career scientists worldwide (within five years of a degree being awarded), emerging conservation practitioners, and community-led initiatives

geography.quote: The Small Grant is designed for short (up to 18 months) and small projects in any country

access.quote: The Small Grant application process consists of a two-stage online application

window.quote: Stage I: is CLOSED and will open again mid-March 2027

co_finance_required.quote: Joint funding/co-funding of a project by SOSF with another funding agency is welcomed, but not essential.

reporting.quote: Upon completion of the project, a final report must be submitted using the SOSF template. The report must include a financial summary accounting for the use of the funds provided and be consistent with SOSF's reporting expectations. The report must be submitted no later than 90 days after the project end date.

effort.quote: Stage I involves completing a short online form, equivalent to two pages.
Stage II, by invitation only based on the Stage I application, will involve the completion of a longer and more detailed online form, equivalent to a maximum of 10 pages.

eligibility.quote: dedicated to early-career scientists worldwide (within five years of a degree being awarded), emerging conservation practitioners, and community-led initiatives
Only projects concerned with marine chondrichthyan species (sharks, rays, skates, sawfishes and chimaeras) will be considered.
Successful applicants for small project grants, including scoping projects, may receive a maximum of two small project grants during their early career.
They are not eligible to apply for a small grant in the year following the award of the first small grant.
Costs for salaries, conference attendance and publications are not accepted.

after_award.quote: One blog per semester, of good-quality "web blogs" which will be posted to the SOSF website on the specific Project page and/or on SOSF social media networks.
The Project Leader shall, given reasonable advance notice, permit SOSF access to the Project so that SOSF may have the opportunity of assessing the progress of the Project

documents.quote: Recent CV for the Project Leader (and co-PL if relevant)
from supervisor if appropriate, otherwise from another person from the institution
